title: When the world changes
summary: Studying how world-model agents revise outdated information when an environment’s physics changes.
question: When physics changes, how does a world-model agent replace outdated information—and can we identify the internal computations responsible for successful or failed adaptation?
abstract: A learned world model can retain assumptions that stop matching its environment. This project asks how an agent responds when the underlying physics changes: which information is retained, which information is replaced, and how those changes affect behavior.

The interpretability question is causal: can we identify the internal computations that distinguish successful adaptation from persistent reliance on outdated information? This is a research question, with the notebook below reserved for future reports and progress checks.
